title: AI-Powered Detection of Inappropriate Language in Medical School Curricula

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using supervised fine-tuning of Small Language Models (DistilBERT, BioBERT) and few-shot prompting of Large Language Models (LLMs) on the BRICC dataset to detect gender misuse and exclusive language (e.g., language assuming gender binaries) in medical educational texts.

Measured by training binary and multilabel classifiers, as well as prompting LLMs, to identify the inappropriate use of biological sex terms (e.g., using 'female' instead of 'woman' for an individual patient case) within clinical curricula.

Assessed by evaluating language models on their ability to detect vague or stigmatizing age-related terminology (e.g., 'the elderly' or 'older individuals') versus objective numerical ranges in medical instructional materials.

Evaluated by testing classifiers on their ability to flag non-patient-centered language (e.g., defining people by their conditions like 'diabetics' instead of 'patients with diabetes') and outdated, stigmatizing clinical terminology (e.g., 'mentally retarded').
